title: Meeting Set At Savoy Tonight After Blaze Destroys Church
text:
FIRE THREATENED TOWN

Meeting Set At Savoy Tonight After Blaze Destroys Church

By ELIZABETH LARGE

SAVOY — A town meeting has been set for the school house at 7:30 p.m. today to start the ball rolling toward getting new fire fighting equipment for Savoy.

Mayor S. A. Bibby called the meeting after discussing the aftermath to the $15,000 fire that destroyed the Savoy Church of Christ Sunday morning.

The blaze, discovered by a passing motorist, at one time threatened the entire town and only the alert work of fire departments from three towns kept at least a half-dozen adjoining dwellings from being destroyed.

Fire trucks from Savoy, Bonham, Trenton, Bells and Sherman answered the alarm.

The fire was discovered about 10 a.m. by an unidentified motorist who went to the church and awakened teacher William Zilliam E. Hallagan, and told him the roof of the building was on fire.

Hallagan quickly passed the word to the Sunday school teacher and of the children's classrooms were speedily evacuated.

The older persons were told of the blaze and they helped get the young ones out, also alerting Hallagan. "There was no panic and no injuries," he stated.

Witnesses said the flames apparently were just waiting for the building to be cleared as the fire fell from the attic into the main auditorium just minutes after it had been emptied.

"It could have been a catastrophe," reported the mayor.

As the fire started spreading to adjoining dwellings the neighboring blocks arrived quickly at the scene. With little chance to save the church, they concentrated on keeping the fire, which was fanned by a stiff breeze, from spreading.

The roofs on the houses of Miss Elizabeth Large, Everett Burris, A. R. Hodges and others had been ignited by the sparks, firemen hosed the roofs and kept a spray of water on them.

Hay in a barn near the church caught on a garage across the street was on fire and minor damages. Dallas man, Mrs. Minnie Hodges, someone reportedly dug the basement with a few shovels at the scene when the fireman [?] arrived at the scene. Mrs. Frances was released with a bruised hand. Chevrolet quickly drove to [?] County Hospital

incidentally, is pastor of the church that burned.

"The people of Savoy are really aroused this time to the need of adequate fire protection," said S. A. Bibby, mayor, who pointed out to the citizens that it had been as high Sunday as it was a day earlier, out entire town could have been wiped out by the fire."

Some of the many faults that occurred were brought out at the meeting. One was the failure to check fire hydrants at intervals. Two wrenches were broken trying to get one hydrant open and firemen were never able to turn on another.

It was also pointed out that the Savoy water tank was no more than two-thirds full at the time of the fire.

The church building had been constructed in 1913 after a storm had blown the old one off its blocks. The original church had been built "sometime after" the Savoy cyclone in 1880. Before the cyclone the church had held its services just south of town in the old Roberts school house.

New furniture, most of which was installed a year or so ago, was lost. All that was saved from the fire was the communion table and service, two large floor fans, four pews, the pulpit stand and two chairs.

A total of $8,000 insurance was carried on the building and its contents, according to J. B. May, who said it probably would take $15,000 to $20,000 to replace it today.

"We will rebuild," said the minister this morning. "As soon as we can get organized we'll start rebuilding."

But meanwhile, all of Savoy was up in arms about the dire need for fire fighting equipment in town and at the town meeting tonight, it is a good bet that something will be done.
notes: Headline flag reads 'FIRE THREATENED TOWN'. Some text in the middle columns is difficult to read; uncertain phrases noted with [?]. The church was the Savoy Church of Christ. Fire damage estimated at $15,000.
